name: Hetzner Cloud
tagline: Low-cost VMs in Germany, Finland and the US
description: SAM's first provider. Connect an API token and SAM creates, reuses and deletes Hetzner VMs for workspaces and app deployments, with block volumes for deployment data.
seoTitle: Run AI Coding Agents on Hetzner Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run AI coding agents on Hetzner Cloud VMs with SAM, the open-source agent platform. SAM provisions, reuses and deletes machines on your Hetzner account.

features.title: Five locations
features.description: Falkenstein, Nuremberg, Helsinki, Ashburn and Hillsboro.

features.title: Token sign-in
features.description: A Hetzner Cloud API token. No IAM setup.

features.title: Persistent volumes
features.description: Deployment environments keep their data on Hetzner volumes that survive node replacement.

howItWorks.description: In the Hetzner Cloud Console, open a project and generate a read-write API token.
Paste the token in Settings → Infrastructure → Cloud accounts.
SAM places agents on existing machines with room, or creates a VM in your chosen location.

useCases.title: Cheap parallel capacity
useCases.description: Run many agent sessions on small, inexpensive machines.

useCases.title: EU data location
useCases.description: Keep machines in Germany or Finland.

faq.question: Do I need my own Hetzner account?
faq.answer: Only if nobody else provides one. SAM uses a project's cloud account first, then yours, then one the installation administrator connected. With none of those, a profile can still run Instant sessions on Cloudflare Containers.

faq.question: How is my credential stored?
faq.answer: Encrypted with AES-256-GCM and a unique IV in your installation's database. Machines never receive it: the control plane makes the provider API calls.

name: Vultr
tagline: Nine locations across Europe, North America, Asia and Australia
description: Connect a Vultr API key and SAM provisions Cloud Compute instances for workspaces and app deployments, with NVMe Block Storage for deployment data in the regions that offer it.
seoTitle: Run AI Coding Agents on Vultr | SAM
seoDescription: Run AI coding agents on Vultr Cloud Compute with SAM, the open-source agent platform. Nine locations across four continents.

features.title: Nine locations
features.description: Frankfurt, Amsterdam, London, New Jersey, Chicago, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Singapore and Sydney.

features.title: Persistent volumes
features.description: NVMe Block Storage, in the subset of Vultr regions that offer it.

features.title: API key sign-in
features.description: A Vultr personal access token.

howItWorks.description: In the Vultr customer portal, open Account → API and generate a personal access token.

howItWorks.step: Allow all IPs on the token
howItWorks.description: SAM calls Vultr from Cloudflare Workers, which have no fixed outbound IP, so an IP allowlist on the token blocks provisioning.
Paste the key in Settings → Infrastructure → Cloud accounts. Frankfurt is the default region.

useCases.title: Machines near your team
useCases.description: Pick a region in North America, Europe, Asia or Australia.

useCases.title: Second provider
useCases.description: Add Vultr next to another provider so a pool can fall back when one runs out of capacity.

faq.question: Why must the token allow all IPs?
faq.answer: SAM provisions from Cloudflare Workers, which have no fixed outbound IP. A token restricted to listed IPs rejects those requests.

faq.question: Roughly what does it cost?
faq.answer: SAM's default Vultr sizes run from about $20 a month (2 vCPU, 4 GB) to $80 a month (6 vCPU, 16 GB), billed hourly by Vultr.

faq.question: Do I need my own Vultr account?
faq.answer: Only if nobody else provides one. SAM uses a project's cloud account first, then yours, then one the installation administrator connected. With none of those, a profile can still run Instant sessions on Cloudflare Containers.

name: Google Cloud
description: Sign in with Google and SAM sets up Workload Identity Federation in your project for you, or connect a service-account key. SAM then provisions Compute Engine VMs.
seoTitle: Run AI Coding Agents on Google Cloud | SAM
seoDescription: Run AI coding agents on Google Compute Engine with SAM, the open-source agent platform. Keyless Workload Identity Federation, set up for you.

features.title: Keyless by default
features.description: Connect with Google and SAM enables the APIs it needs, creates the WIF pool, provider and service account, and grants the bindings in your project.

features.title: Service-account key option
features.description: Where the installation has no Google infrastructure OAuth client, connect a service-account JSON key instead.

features.title: Live machine catalog
features.description: SAM builds its list of machine types and prices from Google's own catalog and billing data.

features.title: Eight zones
features.description: Iowa, South Carolina, Oregon, Belgium, Frankfurt, London, Singapore and Tokyo.

howItWorks.description: In Settings → Infrastructure → Cloud accounts, sign in with a Google account that can administer your VM project.
SAM sets up Workload Identity Federation in that project and verifies the token exchange.
SAM creates Compute Engine VMs with short-lived credentials. The VMs get no service account.

useCases.title: Use existing Google commitments
useCases.description: Run agent machines on a GCP project that already has credits or a billing agreement.

useCases.title: No stored long-lived key
useCases.description: With WIF, SAM exchanges short-lived tokens instead of keeping a service-account key.

faq.question: Does GCP support persistent deployment volumes?
faq.answer: Not yet. A deployment environment on Google Cloud cannot use persistent volumes, so put environments that need them on another provider.

faq.question: What does the installation administrator need to set up?
faq.answer: A Google OAuth client for infrastructure sign-in, with the Cloud Resource Manager and IAM APIs enabled. The Google Cloud guide lists every step.

faq.question: Do I need my own Google Cloud account?
faq.answer: Only if nobody else provides one. SAM uses a project's cloud account first, then yours, then one the installation administrator connected. With none of those, a profile can still run Instant sessions on Cloudflare Containers.
